notes: Instrumentation (keeper heal cooldown). Test-first per the standing TDD rule: wrote the T504 arms in tools/regression-fleet-keeper.sh, ran them against the unmodified keeper, and observed T504-a and T504-e RED (the keeper dispatched the healed T358); then implemented the fix and re-ran green. What was built: tools/fleet-keeper.sh now persists a per-row heal cooldown in untracked/fleet-keeper.heal.json and parks a recently-healed dispatchable row for FLEET_HEAL_COOLDOWN seconds (default 600). Heal signal is read from what T477 already records, not a new source: (1) the dispatcher heal record log docs/infra/dispatch-heals.jsonl (latest timestamp per task), and (2) claim_count>=2 from the kanban store (read directly because `managent status --json` omits claim_count). The cooldown clears on `done` or on window expiry; a NEW heal (newer heal record, or a higher claim_count) restarts it; the exclusion is logged as `heal-cooldown: <id> (healed Ns ago, waiting)`. Controls added: T504-a (claim_count=2 + recent heal -> parked, exclusion logged, persists across iterations), T504-b (expired window -> eligible again), T504-c (fresh row claim_count=1, no heal -> dispatched normally), T504-e (fresh T477 heal record with claim_count=1 -> parked, the live T358 defect shape). Findings on the way: N1 — T503's `least_data_model` change in tools/fleet-keeper.sh is ORPHANED-UNCOMMITTED (T503 is `done`, verdict pass-with-findings, but its seat's commit 01747e5 does not touch fleet-keeper.sh); it is operator-ratified (exploration-first, least-data model) and is preserved in this commit alongside the T504 change. N2 — the T496 arm-1 log check hardcoded `dispatched T1 -> glm-5.2`, which T503's least-data pick (kimi-k2.7) falsified; I made the check model-agnostic (its stated intent is 'log records each firing', not which model). N3 — a leaked FLEET_MODEL_ALLOW/DENY in the caller's env (a DeepSeek carve) denied glm-5.2 and broke every arm's model resolution; the regression now unsets both at the top (it already owns them in arm f).
